stemMd: What is the central point of "Counting the quiet city"?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Volunteer observations should replace all instrument readings.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Useful measurements can still omit important experiences when their locations and times are too limited.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Daily averages always exaggerate short noise events.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Resident measurements show that traffic produces no significant noise.

explanationMd: The passage preserves the value of the first survey while explaining its limitations. Expanding times and routes captures experiences that the original design missed.

distractorRationale.c: The passage says averages can conceal brief peaks rather than exaggerate them.
distractorRationale.d: The new results retain the earlier finding that major roads are loud.
distractorRationale.a: Volunteers themselves use instruments, and roadside monitors will be retained.
